anti_overlap: fd-matchmaking-compatibility-weighting covers scoring structure; fd-ethology-pair-bond-formation covers behavioral sequencing; this covers how the system's outputs are made interpretable to the AI curator tier
decision_lens: Inferential legibility — the system must produce behavioral outputs that allow an informed observer to reconstruct the underlying drivers that produced the relationship
distance_rationale: Attachment theorists have developed rigorous methods for making internal relational states legible from behavioral evidence — exactly the problem the curator faces when explaining elf relationships to the human player.
expected_isomorphisms: Event-linked causal records for attraction deltas map to the clinical practice of noting specific incidents as evidence of attachment pattern. The explain-pairing tool design mirrors structured clinical formulation. Legible attachment patterns (anxious, avoidant, secure) map to named elf relationship archetypes the curator can deploy.
focus: Whether a romantic attraction system is legible to the 'narrator' (curator/AI advisor) — how clinical psychologists make attachment patterns readable from behavioral evidence without direct access to internal states
name: fd-clinical-attachment-legibility
persona: Clinical psychologist specializing in attachment theory who trains therapists to infer attachment style from observable relationship behavior rather than self-report, and who consults on AI systems that must explain relationship dynamics
review_areas: Evaluate whether each attraction driver leaves a distinct behavioral trace that a curator could cite when explaining a pairing — 'these elves bonded because of shared grief at the revel' requires the grief event to be logged and causally linked to the attraction score delta

Check whether the system supports the 'anxious-avoidant' dynamic: elves with high attraction to prestige (status driver) paired with elves who have low prestige-seeking (underdog attraction) should produce a recognizable pattern of pursuit and withdrawal

Assess whether the 'fandom-to-love pipeline' produces a legible narrative transition — the curator should be able to report 'Elf A became a fan of Elf B's work at the autumn revel, and has attended every revel where Elf B performs since', not just 'Elf A has high attraction to Elf B'
Evaluate whether asymmetric attraction (if implemented) is legible — the curator must be able to explain why one elf feels attraction and the other does not, based on their different driver profiles

Check whether the design of the curator's explain-pairing tool is constrained by the attraction driver model — a driver model with 7 independent categories requires a richer explanation template than a 2-3 driver model

severity_examples.condition: Attraction delta events are not logged with causal driver tags
severity_examples.scenario: Attraction scores accumulate correctly but without event-linked causal records — the curator can report 'these elves are highly attracted' but cannot explain why, breaking the core promise of the bead description ('aesthetic proximity + personality complementarity + proximity time' as an explainable formula)

severity_examples.condition: Curator explanation template doesn't enumerate contributing drivers above a threshold weight
severity_examples.scenario: The system supports 7 attraction drivers but the curator's explain-pairing prompt template only surfaces the top 1 — producing 'these elves share aesthetic taste' for every pairing, even when the real driver was skill-gap admiration after the winter composition revel

severity_examples.condition: Continuous/statistical drivers have no discrete event representation in the event log
severity_examples.scenario: Mood resonance driver (elves whose mood curves sync) produces attraction without leaving any observable event in the timeline — the curator cannot point to a moment when the synchrony was established, only an abstract 'their moods tend to align'

source_domain: Clinical psychology, attachment theory, and relational inference
success_hints: When the curator explains why two elves are attracted, the explanation reads like a story, not a formula readout — referencing specific shared events, a named revel where fandom began, or the skill gap that first made an elf look up.
task_context: The brainstorm explicitly names curator legibility as a design tension ('the curator needs to explain pairings'); clinical psychology's methodology for inferring attachment style from behavioral evidence directly addresses this.
